title: Swiggy's quick commerce arm Instamart to let go of 340 employees amid AI push
summary: Swiggy's Instamart to lay off 340 employees amid AI-driven restructuring
detailed: Swiggy is laying off 340 employees from its quick commerce division, Instamart, amid corporate restructuring and rising AI adoption.
The job cuts primarily affect corporate and support functions as the company attempts to address sustained underperformance and widening losses.
Swiggy reported a net loss of Rs 922 crore in Q2 FY27 and maintains cash and cash equivalents of approximately Rs 13,500 crore.
This matters because it highlights ongoing cost-cutting and strategic shifts under new CEO Nandita Sinha to counter intense competition in the quick commerce sector.
sentences: Online food and grocery delivery company Swiggy is set to lay off 340 employees from its quick commerce division, Instamart, as it restructures the business for its next phase of growth, amid a rise in AI adoption, people aware of the developments told Moneycontrol.
The cost-cutting exercise comes as Instamart grapples with sustained underperformance and widening losses for several quarters in a row.
"People largely in teams like corporate and support functions within Instamart have been impacted," one of the persons cited above said.
The company has put in place severance packages, outplacement support and is also providing relocation services.
The move comes amid rising competitive intensity from Eternal-owned Blinkit, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes, Amazon Now and others.
Swiggy, however, remains well capitalised and has cash and cash equivalents of around Rs 13,500 crore.
Instamart, under new CEO Nandita Sinha, is tweaking its strategy and increasing focus on private labels, Moneycontrol had exclusively reported earlier.

ALSO READ: Why Swiggy picked Nandita Sinha, another Flipkart veteran, to lead Instamart's turnaround
In Q2, Swiggy had reported net loss narrowing 15.6 percent year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 922 crore in the second quarter (Q2) of financial year 2026-27 (FY27) from Rs 1,092 crore in the same period a year ago.
The Bengaluru-based firm had reported a loss of Rs 791 crore in the previous quarter, as rapid expansion in its quick commerce vertical Instamart took a toll on the company’s bottom line.
